title: Rational characteristic polynomial of an abelian endomorphism
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] of dimension $g$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Put $E=\operatorname{End}_k(A)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, with composition multiplication and group-scheme endomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every $u\in E$ there is a unique monic polynomial $P_u(X)\in\mathbf Q[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] of degree $2g$ whose image in $\mathbf Q_\ell[X]$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] is $\det(X\,1-V_\ell(u)\mid V_\ell A)$ for every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, with $V_\ell A$ as in [sk-def-av-tate]. For an integral endomorphism $u$, $P_u$ has coefficients in $\mathbf Z$. For $g=0$, $P_u=1$. Characteristic polynomials and determinants use [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial, def-weil-endomorphism-determinant].

source.place: Chapter I, Theorem 10.9 and Remark 10.11, pp.46–48; Proposition 10.20 and proof, pp.50–52. Rational extension by clearing denominators as in Remark 10.11.

proof.text: By [prop-av-tate-rank], $V_\ell A$ has dimension $2g$. If $g=0$, its matrix has size zero, so its determinant polynomial is the empty determinant $1$. Thus $P_u=1$ has all required properties in this case. Henceforth $g>0$.

Put $R=\operatorname{End}_k(A)$ and $E=R\otimes\mathbf Q$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-finite-free], $R$ is finite free, so $E$ is finite-dimensional. It is nonzero: [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-polynomial] gives $\delta(1)=1$ and $\delta(0)=0$ for its rational degree function $\delta=d^0$. The same node makes $\delta$ homogeneous polynomial of degree $2g$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-multiplicative], degree is multiplicative on $R$. For $v=j(a)/n,w=j(b)/m$ from [lem-sfb-rational-tensor-fractions], the degree formula gives $\delta(vw)=(nm)^{-2g}d(ab)=\delta(v)\delta(w)$. Thus $\delta$ satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-polynomial-norm].

source.place: Remark 10.11, Proposition 10.13, printed pp.47–48; Lemma 10.22, printed p.51

proof.text: For $a\in R$, [lem-sfb-multiplicative-polynomial-norm] constructs the monic rational polynomial $P_a(t)=\delta(t1-a)$ of degree $2g$, with its root-product identity. It has integer coefficients: left multiplication $L_a$ acts on the finite free abelian group $R$ of step 2. By [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module], its integral monic characteristic polynomial $H$ annihilates $L_a$; applying $H(L_a)$ to $1$ gives $H(a)=0$. The integral-coefficient clause of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-polynomial-norm] now applies. This does not infer integrality merely from integer values.

source.place: Theorem 10.9 and Remark 10.11, printed pp.46–48; integral-coefficient detail using Theorem 10.15, printed p.49

proof.text:
Fix an allowable $\ell$, set $T=V_\ell(a)$, and let $Q=\det(X1-T)$. By [prop-av-tate-rank] and [lem-weil-charpoly-monic-degree], $Q$ is monic of degree $2g$. Over an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, [p-linear-triangular] supplies a basis making $T$ upper triangular, with diagonal entries $b_i$, the roots of $Q$. For $F\in\mathbf Z[T]$, the matrix $F(T)$ is upper triangular with diagonal $F(b_i)$; its determinant is therefore $\prod_iF(b_i)$. The componentwise definition [sk-def-av-tate] respects sums, composition and integer multiplication, so $F(T)=V_\ell(F(a))$. If $a_i$ are the roots of $P_a$ in the same algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, which is a field extension of $\mathbf Q$ splitting $P_a$, [lem-sfb-multiplicative-polynomial-norm] and [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-tate-valuation] give
$$\left|\prod_iF(a_i)\right|_\ell=|d(F(a))|_\ell=|\det F(T)|_\ell=\left|\prod_iF(b_i)\right|_\ell.$$
Here $F(a)$ is an integral endomorphism and may be a non-isogeny; the valuation node includes that case. Apply [lem-sfb-padic-resultant-rigidity] to conclude $P_a=Q$ after coefficient extension.

source.place: Proposition 10.20, printed pp.50–52, using Lemmas 10.21 and 10.22

proof.text:
For any $u\in E$, choose $n>0$ and $a\in R$ with $nu=j(a)$ by [lem-sfb-rational-tensor-fractions], and define $P_u(X)=n^{-2g}P_a(nX)$. It is monic of degree $2g$ over $\mathbf Q$. For every allowable $\ell$, $V_\ell(u)=n^{-1}V_\ell(a)$ by rational extension of the componentwise action. Factoring $n$ from each of the $2g$ rows gives
$$\det(X1-V_\ell(u))=n^{-2g}\det(nX1-V_\ell(a))=n^{-2g}P_a(nX).$$
For integral $u$ take $n=1$, recovering step 3 and its integer coefficients. No invertibility of $n$ in $k$ is needed, only its invertibility in $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Remark 10.11, printed p.47, rational rescaling formula

proof.text: Choose $\ell=2$ when $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, and $\ell=3$ otherwise. The canonical homomorphism $\mathbf Q\to\mathbf Q_\ell$ is injective by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. If two rational polynomials satisfy the required realizations, their images at this prime agree with the same determinant polynomial, so injectivity on every coefficient makes them equal. This proves uniqueness, and also independence of the choice of denominator in step 5.

source.place: Remark 10.10, printed p.46; uniqueness from one faithful coefficient field

proof_origin.place: Chapter I, Remark 10.11, Proposition 10.13 and Proposition 10.20 with Lemmas 10.21–10.22, printed pp.46–52; explicit integrality, non-isogeny and denominator details
